description: Helios: Real Real-Time Long Video Generation Model

summary.one_liner: Helios is an official open-source 14B video generation model from PKU-YuanGroup that produces minute-scale videos in real time for text-to-video, image-to-video, and video-to-video.
summary.what_it_does: The repository provides the training and inference code and weights for three Helios variants (Base, Mid, and Distilled), which share one architecture. It autoregressively generates video in chunks of 33 frames, and the README reports about 19.5 FPS end-to-end on a single H100 GPU. Inference scripts cover text-to-video, image-to-video, and video-to-video, with an experimental interactive mode. The README documents several ways to run it: the native scripts, Diffusers pipelines (standard and modular), vLLM-Omni, and SGLang-Diffusion. It also describes group offloading (around 6GB VRAM) and context parallelism across multiple GPUs. A three-stage training pipeline and a HeliosBench benchmark are included.
use_cases: generate minute-long videos from text prompts
animate a still image into a video
restyle or transform an existing video with a text prompt
real-time or interactive video generation experiments
run video generation on limited-VRAM GPUs
research and fine-tuning of long-video diffusion models
how_to_run: conda create -n helios python=3.11.2 && conda activate helios
pip install torch==2.10.0 torchvision==0.25.0 torchaudio==2.10.0 --index-url <CUDA-specific PyTorch index>
pip install "huggingface_hub[cli]" && huggingface-cli download BestWishYSH/Helios-Distilled --local-dir BestWishYSH/Helios-Distilled
notable: Claims minute-scale video at about 19.5 FPS on one H100 without common anti-drifting or standard acceleration techniques
Three released checkpoints: Base (best quality), Mid (intermediate), and Distilled (best efficiency)
Supports Group Offloading and several context-parallelism backends (Ulysses, Ring, Unified)
Day-0 support listed for Diffusers, SGLang-Diffusion, vLLM-Omni, and Ascend NPU
Includes training code with DDP or DeepSpeed and a three-stage training pipeline
caveats: Real-time speed depends on hardware; the README reports about 10 FPS on a single Ascend NPU and notes that CPU, memory, and driver versions also matter
Image-to-video and video-to-video may be somewhat weaker than text-to-video because training was based on text-to-video
The interactive feature is still under development and results may not meet expectations
Full inference expects a 14B model and a CUDA-capable GPU; the 6GB figure applies only with group offloading
